§ 111.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ITINERANT MERCHANT. Any person who sells, or offers to sell, in this state,
at wholesale or retail, any personal property and transports the same on any
highway in this state by the use of a motor vehicle.
   PERSON. Any individual, corporation, partnership, association or other legal
entity.
   TEMPORARY OR TRANSIENT BUSINESS. Any business or home improvement service;
siding, roofing or resurfacing services, conducted for the sale or offer for
sale of goods, wares or merchandise which is carried on in any building,
structure, motor vehicle, mobile home, travel trailer, railroad car or real
estate for a period of less than two years.
   TRANSIENT MERCHANT. Any person, firm, corporation, partnership or other
entity which engages in, does or transacts any temporary or transient business
in this state, either in one locality or in traveling from place to place in
this state, offering for sale or selling goods, wares, merchandise or services,
and includes those merchants who, for the purpose of carrying on such business,
hire, lease, use or occupy any building, structure, motor vehicle, railroad car
or real estate.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-1)
§ 111.02 ENFORCEMENT.
   It is the duty of the police officers of the city to examine all places of
business and persons in their respective territories subject to the provisions
of this chapter, to determine if this chapter has been complied with and to
enforce the provisions of this chapter against any person found to be violating
the same.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-2)
§ 111.03 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No transient merchant shall transact business within the city unless such
merchant and the owners of any goods, wares or merchandise to be offered for
sale or sold, if such goods, wares or merchandise are not owned by the
merchant, shall have secured a license and have otherwise complied with the
requirements of this code.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-3) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.04 EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   Specified. The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to:
      (1)   Sales at wholesale to retail merchants by commercial travelers or
selling agents in the usual course of business, to retail merchants in that
line of business;
      (2)   Wholesale trade shows or conventions;
      (3)   Sales of goods, wares or merchandise by sample, catalog or brochure
for future delivery;
      (4)   Fairs and convention center activities conducted primarily for
amusement or entertainment;
      (5)   Any general sale, fair, auction or bazaar sponsored by any church
or religious organization;
      (6)   Any sale sponsored by schools and universities or any charitable
organization;
      (7)   Wholesale trade fairs with no on-site sales and delivery;
      (8)   Garage sales held on the premises devoted to residential use;
      (9)   Sales of crafts or items made by hand and sold or offered for sale
by the person making such crafts or handmade items;
      (10)   Sales of agricultural products grown by the seller;
      (11)   Sales made by a seller at residential premises pursuant to an
invitation issued by the owner or legal occupant of such premises;
      (12)   Any person who maintains a permanent place of business in this
state and has a registered agent therein upon whom process, notice or demand
permitted by law may be made; and
      (13)   Any person whose participation with a transient merchant or in the
temporary or transient business, as defined in §
111.01 of this chapter, is limited to providing any building, structure, motor
vehicle, railroad car or real estate.
   (B)   Association with local business. A transient merchant not otherwise
exempted as set out above, shall not be relieved or exempted from the
provisions of this chapter by reason of associating himself or herself
temporarily with any local dealer, auctioneer, trader, contractor or merchant,
or by conducting such temporary or transient business in connection with or in
the name of any local dealer, auctioneer, trader, contractor or merchant.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-4)
§ 111.05 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   (A)   Required; contents. Any transient merchant desiring to transact
business in the city shall make application for and obtain a license to
transact business. The application for license shall be filed with the City
Clerk at least three business days prior to the transaction of business, and
shall include the following information:
      (1)   The name and permanent address of the transient merchant making the
application, and if the applicant is a firm or corporation, the name and
address of the members of the firm or the officers of the corporation, as the
case may be;
      (2)   If the applicant is a corporation, there shall be stated on the
application form the date of incorporation, the state of incorporation, and if
the applicant is a corporation formed in a state other than this state, the
date on which such corporation qualified to transact business as a foreign
corporation in this state;
      (3)   A statement showing the kind of business proposed to be conducted,
the length of time for which the applicant desires to transact such business
and the location of such proposed place of business;
      (4)   The name and permanent address of the transient merchant’s
registered agent or office; and
      (5)   Proof that the applicant has acquired all other required county and
state permits and licenses. The applicant shall provide to the City Clerk
applicant’s current state and federal tax identification number.
   (B)   Verification by City Clerk. The City Clerk shall verify the validity
of the application within three days of application.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-5)
§ 111.06 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   Each application for a transient/itinerant vendor and transient/itinerant
merchant license shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable license fee of $50.
(Refer to Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-2-6)
§ 111.07 ISSUANCE OF LICENSE; TRANSFERABILITY; VALIDITY.
   (A)   A transient business license shall be issued only when all the
requirements of this chapter have been met.
   (B)   Such license shall not be transferable, shall be valid only within the
territorial limits of the city, and shall be valid only for the business stated
in the application.
   (C)   A license so issued shall be valid for only one person, unless such a
person shall be a member of a partnership or employee of a firm or corporation
obtaining such license.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-7)
§ 111.08 EXPIRATION OF LICENSE.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this chapter shall expire 30
days after the date of issuance thereof, unless a prior date is fixed therein.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-8)
§ 111.09 POSSESSION OF LICENSE REQUIRED.
   Any person receiving a license under this chapter shall have the same in
possession at all times while conducting business.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-9)
§ 111.10 LOUD NOISES AND SPEAKING DEVICES.
   No licensee under this chapter, nor anyone in his or her behalf, shall
shout, make an outcry, blow a horn, ring a bell or use any other sound device,
including any loud speaking radio or amplifying system upon any of the streets,
alleys, parks or other public places of the city, or upon any private premises
in the city where sound of sufficient volume is emitted or produced therefrom
capable of being plainly heard upon the streets, avenues, alleys or parks or
other public places, for the purpose of attracting attention to any goods,
wares or merchandise which such licensee proposes to sell.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-10) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.11 REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   (A)   Causes. The permits and licenses issued pursuant to this chapter may
be revoked by the Mayor after notice and hearing, for any of the following
causes:
      (1)   Any fraud, misrepresentation or false statement contained in the
application for license;
      (2)   Any fraud, misrepresentation or false statement made in connection
with the selling of goods, wares or merchandise;
      (3)   Any violation of this chapter;
      (4)   Conviction of the licensee of any felony or of a misdemeanor
involving moral turpitude; or
      (5)   Conducting the business license under this chapter in an unlawful
manner or in such a manner as to constitute a breach of the peace or to
constitute a menace to the health, safety or general welfare of the public.
   (B)   Hearing; notice. Notice of hearing for revocation of a license shall
be given in writing, setting forth specifically the grounds of the complaint
and the time and place of the hearing. Such notice shall be mailed, postage
prepaid, to the licensee, at his or her last known address, at least five days
prior to the date set for the hearing.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-11)
§ 111.99 PENALTY.
   Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall, upon
conviction thereof, be punished as provided in §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-2-12)
CHAPTER 112: MOBILE FOOD SERVICE ESTABLISHMENTS
Section
   
112.01   Purpose
   
112.02   Definitions
   
112.03   Permit for operation required, offense
   
112.04   Multiple mobile food service permits requirement
   
112.05   Conditions for issuance of permit
   
112.06   Restrictions on locations of operation
   
112.07   Restrictions on location as to time
   
112.08   Possession of valid license and tax permit required
   
112.09   Reasonable conduct of operations
   
112.10   Special events
   
112.11   Use of public property and public rights-of-way
   
112.12   General requirements of operations
   
112.13   Administrative officer designation
   
112.14   Right to appeal
§ 112.01 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate the actions/operations of mobile
food service establishments conducting business operations within the city
limits of the city to the limited and restricted extent as expressly set forth
herein. It is not the purpose of this chapter to adopt “health regulations”
governing or pertaining to mobile food service establishments. The matters of
“health regulations” and enforcement thereof pertaining to mobile food service
establishments are matters the city deems appropriate and in the best interest
of the city to leave to the jurisdiction and control of the State Department of
Health.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-1) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FOOD. A raw, cooked or processed edible substance, ice, beverage or
ingredient used or intended for use or for sale in whole or in part for human
consumption.
   FULL SERVICE MOBILE. A vehicle or trailer designed and equipped to prepare
and serve open food products.
   MOBILE FOOD SERVICE. A facility that prepares or serves food and is vehicle
mounted or is otherwise readily movable and includes, but is not necessarily
limited to, “full service mobile”, “prepackaged mobile” and “pushcart” as those
terms are defined herein.
   PREPACKAGED MOBILE. A vehicle or trailer limited to the sale of commercially
manufactured prepackaged food products.
   PUSHCART. A non-self-propelled vehicle, the operation of which is limited to
serving non- potentially hazardous foods and/or commercially prepackaged foods.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-2) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.03 PERMIT FOR OPERATION REQUIRED, OFFENSE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a mobile food service
within the city limits without a valid mobile food service permit issued by the
city.
   (B)   Violation of this permit requirement shall be an offense and
punishable pursuant to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances.
   (C)   For the purpose of this section, the following definition shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      OPERATE.
         (a)   Physically participating in the active conduct of the operation
of a mobile food service at the location where such activities are occurring;
or
         (b)   A person having the authority to direct and/or manage the
operations of a mobile food service, causing the mobile food service to operate
in violation of this section, regardless of the person being present at the
location where such activities are occurring.
   (D)   There shall be only one form of permit issued by the city regardless
of classification under §
112.02 of this chapter. The permit shall be a permit for mobile food service
establishment.
   (E)   There shall be three classes of permits issued by the city as follows:
      (1)   One day permit (valid for one day specified);
      (2)   Special event permit (valid for duration of time of special event);
and
      (3)   One year permit (valid for calendar year of issuance).
   (F)   The amount of the fee to be paid for the issuance of a permit pursuant
to an approved application for the permit shall be that as set by the City
Council from time to time in Appendix A of this code of ordinances.
   (G)   In addition to the fee for issuance of the permit pursuant to an
approved application as set forth in division (F) of this section there shall
be assessed an administrative processing fee for all applications for permits
in an amount as set by the City Council from time to time in Appendix A of this
code of ordinances.
   (H)   Nonprofit entities shall be exempt from payment of the fee for
issuance of the permit, but shall not be exempt from payment of the fee for
processing of the application for permit.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-3) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 112.04 MULTIPLE MOBILE FOOD SERVICE PERMITS REQUIREMENT.
   A separate mobile food service permit shall be required for each individual
mobile food service unit being operated within the city limits regardless of
common ownership thereof.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-4) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.05 CONDITIONS FOR ISSUANCE OF PERMIT.
   No mobile food service permit will be issued by the city to an applicant
unless and until the applicant satisfies the following conditions of issuance:
   (A)   Provides to the city a copy of the applicant’s approved “application
for food or lodging establishment license” issued by the State Department of
Health;
   (B)   Provides to the city a copy of the applicant’s current, valid state
sales tax permit;
   (C)   An applicant for issuance of a permit under the status of a nonprofit,
charitable or religious organization shall provide official written proof of
exemption from the requirement of collecting sales tax in lieu of the
requirement of a valid state sales tax permit;
   (D)   An applicant for issuance of a permit under the status of a nonprofit,
charitable or religious organization shall not be relieved of the obligation to
provide a copy of the applicant’s approved “application for food or lodging
establishment license” issued by the State Department of Health;
   (E)   Provision to the city of a completed application for mobile food
service permit on the application form prescribed by the city;
   (F)   Payment of the prescribed fees to the city for processing the
application for permit and for issuance of a mobile food service permit
pursuant to an approved application as set forth in
Appendix A of this code of ordinances; and
   (G)   Approval of the application for mobile food service permit by the
city.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-5) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.06 RESTRICTIONS ON LOCATIONS OF OPERATION.
   (A)   Mobile food service operations shall be conducted in conformance with
the restrictions as set forth in this section.
   (B)   A first time violation under division (C)(2), (C)(3), (C)(4), (C)(5)
or (C)(6) of this section shall subject the violator to a written warning which
may be issued by a city law enforcement officer or other appropriate city
official as may be designated by the City Council to issue such warnings.
   (C)   A second violation of division (C)(2), (C)(3), (C)(4), (C)(5) or (C)
(6) of this section which occurs within 60 days of the issuance of a warning
for any violation of any of the aforesaid division (C)(2), (C)(3), (C)(4), (C)
(5) or (C)(6) shall result in the issuance of a ticket by city law enforcement
and shall be deemed an offense punishable pursuant to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances and shall further serve as sufficient grounds
for revocation by the city of the mobile food services permit issued by the
city at the discretion of the city.
      (1)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations
within areas designated by the city’s zoning code as a “residential district”
where such location or conduct of business operations involves the stationary
parking or placement of the mobile food service in one location for a period of
time exceeding ten minutes. Violation of this provision shall constitute an
offense upon the occurrence of the first violation and shall further serve as
sufficient grounds for revocation by the city of the mobile food services
permit issued by the city at the discretion of the city.
      (2)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations in
such a location or in such a manner as to unreasonably inhibit the flow of
traffic upon the city streets, public use of sidewalks, or public access to
alleys as determined in the discretion of the city or city or state law
enforcement personnel.
      (3)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations in
such a location or in such a manner as to inhibit the public access to public
parking as determined in the discretion of the city or city or state law
enforcement personnel.
      (4)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations in
such a location or in such a manner as to inhibit the public access to public
parking as determined in the discretion of the city or city or state law
enforcement personnel.
      (5)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations in
such a location or in such a manner as to pose a danger, risk or threat to the
public safety as determined in the discretion of the city or city or state law
enforcement personnel.
      (6)   No mobile food service may locate or conduct business operations
upon private property located within the city without the permission of the
owner or other person in authority over the private property.
      (7)   No customer shall be served on the street side of the mobile unit.
All service must be on the curb side when the mobile unit is on or abutting a
public street.
      (8)   No drive-through or drive-by customer service shall be provided or
permitted as part of a mobile food service as contemplated in this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-6) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 112.07 RESTRICTIONS ON LOCATION AS TO TIME.
   (A) No mobile food service may remain located at the same location for more
than 12 hours during any single 24-hour period of time.
   (B) No mobile food service may be located at the same location more than 90
days, whether consecutive or not, during any calendar year.
(Ord. 2024-4, passed 6-4-2024) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 112.08 POSSESSION OF VALID LICENSE AND TAX PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   At all times of operation a mobile food service must maintain and have
in its possession a copy of its current and valid food or lodging establishment
license issued by the State Department of Health and state sales tax permit and
mobile food services permit issued by the city.
   (B)   A mobile food service operating within the city limits shall be
obligated to produce copies of the licenses and permits identified in division
(A) of this section for inspection immediately upon request by city law
enforcement officers or officials.
   (C)   The failure to comply with the requirements of this section shall
constitute an offense punishable pursuant to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances and shall further serve as sufficient grounds
for revocation by the city of the mobile food services permit issued by the
city at the discretion of the city.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-8) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 112.09 REASONABLE CONDUCT OF OPERATIONS.
   The conduct of the operation of the mobile food service shall be made and
conducted in such a manner as to not be unreasonably disruptive or offensive to
the peace, health, safety and welfare of the public. Loud music, disruptive
lights and other such activities as may disrupt or offend the peace, health,
safety and welfare of the public are prohibited.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-9) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 112.10 SPECIAL EVENTS.
   At the discretion of the city special exceptions or deviations from the
provisions of §§
112.06 (concerning locations) and
112.07 (concerning time) of this chapter may be allowed for special events or
special circumstances. Deviation or exception from other provisions of this
chapter shall not be allowed. Any such exception or deviation shall be made in
advance of the occurrence of the special event or special circumstance by
unilateral action initiated by the City Council or upon advance approval of the
city pursuant to an application by the person seeking the deviation or
exception. Deviations or exceptions shall not be retroactively allowed,
approved or valid.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-10) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.11 USE OF PUBLIC PROPERTY AND PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY.
   Use of public property and public rights-of-way for the conduct of mobile
food service operations shall be allowed as follows:
   (A)   Use of public streets and rights-of-way is allowed when carried out in
compliance with the provisions of this chapter; and
   (B)   Use of public property such as parks or other public areas may be
allowed when approved in advance by the city.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-11) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.12 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS OF OPERATIONS.
   (A)   All mobile food service operations shall provide garbage receptacles
for customer use.
   (B)   At the conclusion of business activities at a given location the
mobile food service vendor shall clean all the area surrounding his or her
location of all debris, trash and litter generated by the vendor’s business
activities.
   (C)   All mobile food service vendors preparing food by cooking, frying or
other means shall be equipped with at least one fire extinguisher with a
minimum rating of 2A-40-BC.
   (D)   All electrical connections by mobile food service vendors shall fully
comply with requirements of the National Electrical Code (NEC).
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-12) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.13 ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER DESIGNATION.
   The City Council shall designate an administrative officer or administrative
officers of the city whom shall be designated by the City Council to be
possessed of the authority to carry out the powers, duties and authorities of
the city as set forth in this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-13) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
§ 112.14 RIGHT TO APPEAL.
   Any person alleged to be aggrieved by a decision of an administrative
officer designated by the city to act under §
112.13 of this chapter shall have a right of appeal of the decision of the
administrative officer. Appeals under this chapter shall be to the City Council
under the procedures prescribed by this code for administrative appeals in
general.
(Prior Code, § 3-2A-14) (Ord. 2016-3, passed 11-1-2016)
CHAPTER 113: RESIDENTIAL SALES AND AUCTIONS
Section
   
113.01   Residential sales
   
113.02   Auctions
   
113.03   Signage
§ 113.01 RESIDENTIAL SALES.
   (A)   Defined. For the purpose of this section, the following definition
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      RESIDENTIAL SALES. Any sale which is held out to be or commonly known as
a garage, porch, room, yard, neighborhood or driveway sale, or any other type
of general sale conducted from or upon premises not located in a zoning
district which permits such sales, where goods or articles of any type are held
out for sale to the public.
   (B)   Period of sale restricted. No person shall hold or conduct, nor shall
any owner or tenant of any parcel of real property permit the holding or
conducting of, any residential sale which lasts more than two consecutive days
or oftener than once for any one month period of time at the same location or
upon the same premises.
   (C)   Estate and court ordered sales exempt. The provisions of this section
shall not apply to or affect sales conducted in connection with the
administration or closing of estates of deceased persons or sales conducted
pursuant to an order or decree of a court of competent jurisdiction.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-1)
§ 113.02 AUCTIONS.
   (A)   License required. Before any person shall sell or expose for sale, at
public or private auction in this city, any bankrupt or other stock of goods,
wares or merchandise or shall sell or offer for sale any merchandise of any
character whatsoever in this city at public or private auction, the owner
thereof shall first pay to this city a license fee for each day such goods,
wares or merchandise is to be sold or offered for sale in this city. (See
Appendix A of this code of ordinances.)
   (B)   Exemption. Exempt from the license fee requirement are those
individuals or businesses conducting at least three auctions per calendar month
at a permanent location within the city in an area zoned general commercial
district, light industrial district or heavy industrial district.
   (C)   Application for license. Any person desiring to sell or to offer for
sale any of the goods, wares or merchandise at auction in this city under the
provisions of division (A) of this section, shall make application to the City
Clerk, in writing, specifying the name of the owner of the goods, wares or
merchandise to be sold or exposed for sale, the character of the same and the
name of the person proposing to carry on the business, and the place where the
business is to be carried on, and the length of time such auction business is
to be conducted.
   (D)   Solicitation of orders. It is unlawful for any person to solicit
orders for, solicit the purchase of, or otherwise attempt to sell any goods or
services or to solicit appointments for such purposes either in person, by
telephone or otherwise at any place of residence within the city after 7:00
p.m. of any day, unless the person soliciting such orders, purchases or
appointments has previously obtained an appointment with the occupants of such
place of residence and their consent to solicit such purchases or orders at the
approximate time involved.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-2) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 113.03 SIGNAGE.
   A residential sale, auction, estate and court ordered exempt sales sign must
provide location, date, time of sale and shall not remain for greater than 24
hours after close of sale. Any sign placed not in compliance herewith or which
remains longer than 24 hours after the close of the sale shall be considered a
public nuisance and subject to action as provided by law.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-3) (Ord. 2010-3, passed 2-16-2010)

**** FAMILY AMUSEMENT CENTERS ****
§ 114.01 DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definition shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FAMILY AMUSEMENT CENTER. A room or place designed and operated to furnish
recreation for families for a profit offering pool and billiards and similar
games to persons of all ages and either sex and in which are located two or
more pool, billiard or similar tables. No place shall qualify as a FAMILY
AMUSEMENT CENTER where intoxicating liquors and nonintoxicating alcoholic
beverages are sold or offered for sale.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-1)
§ 114.02 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   Authority. The establishment and operation of family amusement centers
in the city is hereby authorized and permitted with the passage of the
ordinance codified herein, subject to the obtaining of a license therefor and
the regulations herein contained.
   (B)   Separate and distinct businesses. Pool halls and family amusement
centers, as defined by the ordinances of the city, shall be considered as
separate and distinct businesses. Any person qualifying and obtaining a license
for either shall not be required to obtain a license for the other.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-2)
§ 114.03 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   (A)   Every person desiring a license for a family amusement center shall
make written application therefor and file the same with the City Clerk,
together with the license fee required by this subchapter.
   (B)   The information required on the application, except for the type of
business for which a license is sought, and the procedure for licensing the
same and the qualifications of the owner or operator of a family amusement
center, shall be the same as that set out for pool halls under the ordinances
of the city.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-3)
Cross-reference:
   Pool and Billiards, see §§
114.40 through
114.45
§ 114.04 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   (A)   Required; term. Every license issued for a family amusement center
shall expire on April 30 of each year. The annual fee for such a license shall
be as set by the City Council by motion or resolution. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
   (B)   Each location. An annual fee shall be required for each location of a
family amusement center. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-4)
§ 114.05 ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   The license required for family amusement centers shall be issued by the
City Clerk by and with the consent of the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-5)
§ 114.06 OPERATING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Generally described. Family amusement centers may operate pool,
billiard and similar tables for a profit and for the use of all ages and either
sex. No beer or other forms of intoxicating liquors or nonintoxicating
alcoholic beverages may be sold, consumed or permitted on the premises. No
gambling or wagering of any kind shall be permitted on the premises. Coin-
operated music or amusement machines may be installed and operated in family
amusement centers and such machines shall not give as a bonus more than five
free games and no cash refund for free games shall be made. Each amusement
machine must bear a state and city license showing that such license fees have
been paid for the period of operation. All such family amusement centers shall
not open before 8:00 a.m. or remain open later than 12:00 midnight, except that
on Sunday, such places of business shall not open before 1:30 p.m. and shall
close by 5:30 p.m.
   (B)   Lighting; glass front. Each family amusement center shall be well
lighted and shall have an open glass front so as to permit open vision from the
outside of the center.
   (C)   Admissions during school hours. No owner, operator, manager or
employee of a family amusement center shall permit any youth 16 years of age or
less to be in or about such establishment during school hours when public
schools are in session.
   (D)   Pool and billiard tables; license required. It shall be unlawful for
any person to operate a place of business where two or more pool, billiard or
similar tables are operated for a profit unless a license therefor is obtained
either for a family amusement center or a pool hall.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-6) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 114.07 REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   The Mayor and City Council may revoke the license of any person to operate a
family amusement center and such revocation shall operate to close such family
amusement center under the license upon any of the following grounds:
   (A)   Violation of subchapter. Violation of the provisions of this
subchapter; and
   (B)   Conduct. Any conduct on the part of the owner, lessee or agent,
servant or employee engaged in the management, conduct, operation or carrying
on of said business which evidences bad moral character.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-7)
**** COIN-OPERATED AMUSEMENT DEVICES ****
§ 114.20 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COIN-OPERATED AMUSEMENT DEVICE.
      (1)   Includes any and all mechanical devices which, upon the payment or
insertion of a coin, token or similar object, causes or permits, or is the
incentive for, the propelling or motivating of any ball, marble or other gadget
or object that produces or creates or makes possible the production or creation
of a game of skill, amusement, entertainment or test of strength; and
      (2)   Does not include any coin-operated music or music device or coin-
operated vending machines used exclusively for the purpose of selling tangible
personal property such as cold drinks, tobacco products, candies, postage
stamps or other merchandise; or services such as pay telephone booths, parking
meters, gas and electric meters or other distribution of needful service.
   PERSON. Includes any individual, partnership, association or corporation.
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-1)
§ 114.21 CLASSIFICATION; ANNUAL TAX.
   Coin-operated amusement devices are hereby classified for the purpose of
taxation and an annual license tax as hereinafter set out is hereby levied with
respect to each such device. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-2)
§ 114.22 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   General. Any owner of a coin-operated amusement device who places such
device in operation or in a place available to the public for operation, and
any person who permits such a device to be in operation or accessible to the
public for operation in his or her place of business, without a license affixed
as required by this subchapter, shall be liable for the tax on such device at
the full annual rate as herein levied and shall be liable to a penalty in
addition to the amount of the tax, in an amount equaling the amount of said
license fee due on such device.
   (B)   Special. In those instances where it is shown to the satisfaction of
the City Clerk that a device, upon which a tax is in this subchapter levied,
will be placed available for use by the public for a definite but limited
period of time less than one year, such as where displayed in connection with
fairs, carnivals and places of amusement that operate only during certain
seasons of the year, the City Clerk may issue a special license therefor. Such
special license may be issued for any number of 30-day periods less than a full
year, and shall indicate that it is a special license; and shall be for one or
more 30-day periods and shall state the precise dates for which issued and
shall not be transferred from one machine to another. The tax shall be computed
and paid on the basis of one-tenth of the annual rate for the type of device
licensed, for each 30-day period for which such special license is issued. In
the event the mechanical device is made available to the public for a period
beyond that for which the special license is issued, then a full year’s tax
shall be due. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-3) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 114.23 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   Any person owning a coin-operated amusement device or operating the premises
where the same is to be operated or exposed to the public, may apply to the
City Clerk for a license for such device and shall at the same time pay to the
City Clerk the annual license tax herein levied. The City Clerk shall, upon
receipt of such payment and approval of such application, issue a license for
the type of device covered by such application and payment. Any number of
machines may be included in one application. Before any coin-operated amusement
device is put in operation or placed where the same may be operated by any of
the public and at all times when the same is being operated or available to any
of the public for operation, a license shall be firmly affixed to the device
covered thereby and plainly visible to and readable by the public.
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-4)
§ 114.24 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   (A)   Enumerated. Every person who owns and has available to any of the
public for operation, or who permits to be operated in or on his or her place
of business, any coin-operated amusement device, shall pay for such privilege
an annual license tax as set by the City Council for each such device. (Refer
to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
   (B)   Taxable year. For the purpose of this subchapter, the taxable year
shall begin on July 1 and end on June 30 and shall be divided into four
quarters. The City Clerk shall in each instance issue a license for the
remainder of the taxable year upon payment of the tax on the basis of the
current and remaining quarters.
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-5)
§ 114.25 ILLEGAL DEVICES.
   Nothing in this subchapter shall be construed to legalize any device that
may be prohibited by any of the statutes of the state or the ordinances of the
city. The City Clerk may assume that any device described in any application
and for which a license tax is paid, is lawful and no claim for refund of any
such license tax shall be entertained based on an owner’s inability to operate
such device because of any law of this state or this city, or for any other
reason.
(Prior Code, § 3-4B-6)
**** POOL AND BILLIARDS ****
§ 114.40 DEFINITION.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definition shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   OPERATE or OPERATES. As used in this subchapter, or any other sections or
ordinances pertaining to a pool, billiard or domino hall, means the taking of
any active part in the management, conducting or carrying on of any business
pertaining to a pool table, billiard table or domino table, either for himself
or herself or as agent, servant or employee of another, whether serving with or
without pay.
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-1)
§ 114.41 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to set up, operate or conduct or permit
to be set up, operated and/or conducted in or about any place of business
within the city, whether for himself or herself as owner, lessee or otherwise,
or as an agent, servant or employee of another, whether serving with or without
pay, two or more pool tables, billiard tables or domino tables, or combination
of the same, for the purpose or purposes of having or allowing the same to be
played by the public for a fee or for profit to the owner of said business or
to the operator without having first obtained a license as hereinafter
provided. Only one license shall be required for each place of business.
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-2) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 114.42 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   The provisions of this subchapter shall apply to all present, future or
pending applications for a pool, billiard or domino hall license and to all
renewals thereof, and shall require that all such applications shall include
the names of all persons who will take part in the management, operation or
conduct of the business in question and their approval by the Mayor and City
Council as hereinafter provided.
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-3)
§ 114.43 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   The annual fee as set by the City Council shall be paid for five tables and
for each additional table. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-4)
§ 114.44 AGE LIMIT AND TIME OF OPERATION.
   No person under the age of 18 years shall be permitted to play pool,
dominos, billiards or checkers in the pool, domino or billiard hall, unless
accompanied by parent or guardian, nor shall they be allowed to work in said
pool, billiard or domino hall. No such hall shall operate between 12:00
midnight and 7:00 a.m. on any day, nor on the Sabbath, with the exception that
recreation centers containing pool or billiard tables, but not containing
domino tables or similar tables may be opened and operated under the provisions
of this subchapter between the hours of 1:00 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. on Sundays.
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-5)
§ 114.45 REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   (A)   The Mayor and City Council may revoke the license of any person to
operate a pool, billiard or domino hall and such revocation shall operate to
close any pool, billiard or domino hall under the license upon the grounds set
out in this subchapter.
   (B)   The following are grounds for revocation or suspension:
      (1)   Violation of subchapter. Violation of any of the provisions of this
subchapter;
      (2)   Intoxication. Drunkenness of the person holding such license,
including any agent, servant or employee taking any active part in the
management, conducting or carrying on of such business, or permitting any
intoxicated person to loiter in such business;
      (3)   Minors. Permitting persons prohibited by ordinances of the city by
reason of age to resort to such place of business, unless accompanied by parent
or guardian;
      (4)   State laws. Violation of any of the laws of the state pertaining to
intoxicating or nonintoxicating liquors, or violation of any of the laws of the
state in or about such place of business by the owner or lessee thereof or any
person engaged in the management, operation, conducting or carrying on of such
business or permitting anyone to violate such laws in said place of business;
and
      (5)   Conduct. Any conduct on the part of the owner, lessee or agent,
servant or employee engaged in the management, conduct, operation or carrying
on of said business which evidences bad moral character.
(Prior Code, § 3-4C-6)
CHAPTER 115: PAWNBROKERS
Section
   
115.01   Defined
   
115.02   Regulatory fee required
   
115.03   Register required
   
115.04   Purchasing certain property prohibited
   
115.05   Sales of property; pledge
§ 115.01 DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definition shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PAWNBROKER. Any person who loans money on deposits of personal property or
who deals in the purchase of personal property on the condition of selling the
same back again at a stipulated price, or who makes a public display at his or
her place of business of the sign generally used by pawnbrokers to denote their
business: three gilt or yellow balls
(Prior Code, § 3-5-1)
§ 115.02 REGULATORY FEE REQUIRED.
   No person shall carry on or engage in business as a pawnbroker without
having first paid to the city a regulatory fee in the sum as set by the City
Council. The regulatory fee shall be paid annually and shall be paid at the
office of the City Clerk. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-5-2) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 115.03 REGISTER REQUIRED.
   (A)   Contents. Every pawnbroker shall keep at his or her place of business
a register in which he or she shall enter in writing a minute description of
all property taken, purchased or received by him or her, including any number
that may be in or upon any article, together with the time and name and place
of residence (giving street and number, if within the city) of the person
leaving the property, also the amount loaned, the interest charged and the time
when the loan falls due; which register shall be kept clean and legible. He or
she shall make such entry within one hour after the receipt or purchase of such
property.
   (B)   Ink entry. Every entry shall be made in ink and shall not in any
manner be obliterated or erased.
   (C)   Ticket. To the person negotiating or leaving such property, he or she
shall give a plainly written or printed ticket, having upon it a full and
perfect copy of all the entries required by ordinance to be kept in such
register, for which copy no charge shall be made.
   (D)   Deliver to Chief of Police. It is the further duty of every pawnbroker
to make out and deliver to the Chief of Police every day a legible and correct
copy from the register of all personal property or other valuable things
received or deposited or purchased during the preceding week, together with the
time when received or purchased and a description of the person by whom left or
from whom the same was purchased.
   (E)   Property purchased from manufactures, dealers. No person shall be
required to furnish such description of any property purchased from
manufacturers or wholesale dealers having an established place of business or
of any goods purchased at open sale or from any bankrupt stock, or from any
other person having an established place of business. But such goods must be
accompanied by a bill of sale or other evidence of open and legitimate
purchase, and must be shown to any officer when demanded.
   (F)   Open to inspection. The register so kept by the person shall at all
times be kept open to the inspection of the Chief of Police and Sheriff of
Mayes County or the deputy of either, any officer of the police force of the
city, the City Attorney and the Prosecuting Attorney of the county, and anyone
authorized in writing for that purpose by the Chief or Captain of the police
force, which authority shall be exhibited to the pawnbroker. The pawnbroker
shall, upon request, show and exhibit to such person or officer for inspection,
any article purchased, taken or received by him or her.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-3)
§ 115.04 PURCHASING CERTAIN PROPERTY PROHIBITED.
   No pawnbroker shall purchase, take or receive in pledge or on deposit, any
article or property of or from a minor, or owned by any minor, or from any
common drunkard or person under the influence of intoxicating liquors or drugs,
or stolen property or property which for any cause, he or she may have reason
to believe or suspect cannot be lawfully or rightfully sold, pawned or pledged
by the person offering it.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-4) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 115.05 SALES OF PROPERTY; PLEDGE.
   (A)   Twenty-four hours. No personal property received on pledge by any
pawnbroker shall be sold or permitted to be redeemed from the place of business
of such pawnbroker for the space of 24 hours after the copy and statement
required to be delivered to the Chief of Police shall have been delivered as
required by §
115.03(D) of this chapter.
   (B)   Before default. No pawnbroker shall sell any article received by him
or her in pledge before the time to redeem has expired.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-5) Penalty, see §
110.99
CHAPTER 116: JUNK AND JUNKYARDS
Section
   
116.01   Definitions
   
116.02   Application to junk motor vehicles
   
116.03   Restriction and prohibition on establishment
   
116.04   Application for license
   
116.05   Fee for license
   
116.06   Rules and requirements
§ 116.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   JUNK. All kinds of previously used or secondhand rags, sacks, bottles, cans,
paper, metal and used or damaged automobiles or other vehicles or machinery not
in running condition or not suitable economically to be repaired or restored to
their original use, or used or damaged automobiles, vehicles or other machinery
purchased, acquired or used for salvage purposes for the benefit of the metal,
material or parts therein contained in whole or in part, and all other articles
of whatsoever nature or kind, commonly purchased after primary use and kept or
sold for subsequent use, consumption or traffic, and otherwise commonly known
as JUNK.
   JUNK DEALER. Any person, firm or corporation, or agent, employee or servant
thereof, engaged in the business of buying, selling or offering for sale or
trade, or otherwise dealing in junk, including the storing or the displaying of
junk or the dismantling, stripping or removal of parts from used automobiles or
other vehicles or machinery in whole or in part for the benefit of the metal,
materials or parts therein contained or stripped. Automobile and tire dealers
who receive or accept used automobiles or tires as down payment or part payment
upon commodities handled by them shall not be included within the terms of this
chapter, provided, however, in the case of automobile dealers, that such used
automobiles are not dismantled or stripped in whole or in part by such
automobile dealer for the purpose of obtaining the metal, material, salvage or
parts therefrom.
   JUNK MOTOR VEHICLE. Includes all automobiles, trucks or other motor vehicles
in such used or damaged condition as not to be economically suitable to be
repaired and restored to their original intended use; all automobiles, trucks
or other motor vehicles from which the metals, materials or parts have been or
are being removed for other use and all automobiles, trucks or other motor
vehicles which are not in operating condition, unless such latter automobiles,
trucks or other motor vehicles are actually being repaired by or on behalf of
the owner thereof within the time reasonably required for the repair of the
same after they have ceased to operate. Any automobile, truck or other motor
vehicle which is required by law to bear and display a license tag and which is
not in safe operating condition and does not bear and display a current license
tag as required by law shall be presumed to be a JUNK MOTOR VEHICLE.
   JUNKYARD. Any place where “junk”, as defined herein, is dismantled or
stripped in whole or in part, bought, sold, stored, displayed or otherwise
dealt with by a junk dealer.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-1)
§ 116.02 APPLICATION TO JUNK MOTOR VEHICLES.
   It is unlawful for any person to park and leave standing upon any public or
private property within view of the public or persons living nearby, or to
permit to be parked and left standing upon any private property under his or
her possession or control within view of the public or persons living nearby,
any junk motor vehicle, except for such time as may be reasonably required to
cause the same to be removed. The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to
junk motor vehicles parked and left standing at any place of business
authorized by law to deal with, store or repair such motor vehicles and which
is operating in compliance with the zoning ordinances and other ordinances of
the city.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-2) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 116.03 RESTRICTION AND PROHIBITION ON ESTABLISHMENT.
   No new junkyard shall be established within the corporate limits of the
city. This prohibition shall not apply to junkyards existing in areas which may
subsequently be annexed within the municipal boundaries. Such preexisting
junkyards in annexed areas shall, upon annexation, secure the license for
operation, and shall comply with the other provisions of this chapter within
the time limits from the date of such annexation as are granted to junkyards
existing within the city upon the initial effective date hereof.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-3) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 116.04 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   Application for a license to operate a junkyard shall be made to the City
Clerk on forms provided by him or her. The application shall contain the name
of the junk dealer, the location of the junkyard or business, and such other
information as the Mayor and City Council may from time to time require.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-4)
§ 116.05 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   For the operation of a business of dealing in junk, the license fee for each
junk dealer shall be as set by the City Council per year. The license shall
expire on April 30 of each year and the license fee therefor, for the initial
application, may be prorated upon a quarterly basis. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-6-5)
§ 116.06 RULES AND REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Yard wall. In any case where a junkyard is operated in a yard or open
space outside of any building, it shall be the duty of the operator or
proprietor to erect and maintain a solid fence, not less than seven feet high,
entirely around the premises where junk is stored, displayed or visible. The
fence shall be made of new, noncombustible materials, sightly in appearance. It
shall be kept in good repair at all times. Junk shall be piled in such manner
within the junkyard as not to be visible from the street or alley upon which
such yard abuts, nor from the ground floor of residential or business property
which may be adjacent thereto. Any junkyard which exists on the effective date
hereof is given a period of 30 days within which to comply with the yard wall
requirements herein set forth.
   (B)   Register of property. Each junkyard operator shall maintain a
register, in which he or she shall enter the item or items which he or she
acquires in the course of trading, for sale or trade, showing its true
character, sufficient for purposes of identification, the person from whom
acquired and the date on which acquired. He or she shall make such entry within
two hours of receiving or purchasing the property. Every entry shall be made in
ink and shall not in any manner be obliterated or erased.
   (C)   Register subject to inspection. The register herein required and any
goods, wares and merchandise which such junk dealer may acquire in the course
of his or her business and offers for sale or trade, shall be subject to the
inspection of the Chief of Police, the City Attorney, the County Attorney and
anyone authorized in writing by the Chief of Police, which authorization shall
be exhibited to the junkyard dealer before inspection is made.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-6)
CHAPTER 117: TREE TRIMMERS LICENSING
Section
   
117.01   Permit required
   
117.02   Residents; exemption
   
117.03   Qualifications; fee; issuance
   
117.04   Employees and agents
   
117.05   Revocation of permit; appeal
§ 117.01 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall engage in the business or occupation of pruning or trimming
of trees on streets, alleys, public lands or public ways within the city
without having first obtained a permit therefor.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-1) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 117.02 RESIDENTS; EXEMPTION.
   Nothing herein shall prohibit the resident of any property from trimming or
pruning the trees or shrubs, personally, upon those premises upon which he or
she resides. Likewise, no permit shall be required for the operations described
in this section.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-2)
§ 117.03 QUALIFICATIONS; FEE; ISSUANCE.
   Any person who holds a valid license as a pruner issued by the State
Department of Agriculture under applicable state law shall be eligible to
qualify for a tree trimmer’s permit. Upon presentation of a state license, the
City Clerk shall issue the permit for an annual fee from May 1 to April 30 of
each year, upon the applicant’s payment of the fee as set by the City Council.
The holder of such permit shall maintain constant, personal supervision of any
employee then engaged in trimming trees. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-7-3)
§ 117.04 EMPLOYEES AND AGENTS.
   The requirement of satisfactorily complying with the city’s regulations
hereunder shall be met by the employees of the city and of its agencies.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-4)
§ 117.05 REVOCATION OF PERMIT; APPEAL.
   At any time, upon noncompliance with its regulation, or for moral
improvidence, the Park Board, or any of its members, may revoke the tree
trimmer’s permit, provided, any tree trimmer whose permit has been so revoked
may appeal such revocation to the City Council to be heard at the next regular
meeting of the City Council after such revocation. The City Council may vacate
such revocation, affirm the same or impose conditions thereto.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-5)
CHAPTER 118: SELF-SERVICE GASOLINE STATIONS
Section
   
118.01   Definitions
   
118.02   Attendant
   
118.03   Dispensing
   
118.04   Spillage; design requirements
   
118.05   Signs for operating instructions and warning
   
118.06   Emergency controls
   
118.07   Storage of liquid wastes
   
118.08   Provisions supplemental
§ 118.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   LIQUID. Any flammable and combustible liquid used as motor fuel or
otherwise.
   SELF-SERVICE STATION. That portion of property where liquids are stored and
subsequently dispensed from fixed approved dispensing equipment by persons,
other than a service station attendant, and may include facilities available
for sale of other retail products.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-1)
§ 118.02 ATTENDANT.
   (A)   Required. A self-service station shall have at least one attendant on
duty while the self-service station is open to the public. The attendant shall
be mentally and physically capable of performing the functions and assuming the
responsibilities prescribed to him or her in this chapter.
   (B)   Duties. Any attendant at a self-service station shall supervise,
observe and control the dispensing of liquid while such liquids are actually
being dispensed. He or she shall prevent the dispensing of liquids into a
portable container unless the container is of metal or is approved by the
office of the State Fire Marshal, has a tight closure with screwed or spring
cover, and is fitted or so designed that the contents can be poured without
spilling. The attendant shall control sources of ignition and immediately
handle accidental spills and fire extinguishers, if needed.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-2)
§ 118.03 DISPENSING.
   (A)   Area; clear view. The dispensing area shall at all times be in clear
view of the attendant and the placing or allowing of any obstacle to come
between the dispensing area and the attendant control area shall be prohibited.
The attendant shall at all times have voice communication with any person in
the dispensing area.
   (B)   Devices. Approved special dispensing devices, such as, but not limited
to, coin-operated and remote-controlled types, are permitted at a self-service
station.
   (C)   Hose nozzle valves. Hose nozzle valves used at a self-service station
shall be an approved automatic closing-type, without a latch-open device.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-3)
§ 118.04 SPILLAGE; DESIGN REQUIREMENTS.
   Provisions shall be made in the area where liquids are dispensed to prevent
spilled liquid from flowing into the interior of self-service station
buildings. Such provision may be made by grading driveways, raising door sills
or other equally effective means.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-4)
§ 118.05 SIGNS FOR OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND WARNING.
   Operating instructions and warning signs shall be conspicuously posted in
the dispensing area. Warning signs shall read: “It is unlawful and dangerous to
dispense gasoline into unapproved containers. No smoking. Turn off engine.”
(Prior Code, § 3-8-5)
§ 118.06 EMERGENCY CONTROLS.
   In a self-service station, emergency controls shall be installed at a
location acceptable to the department having jurisdiction, and shall not be
more than 100 feet from the dispensers. The emergency controls shall be clearly
identified and easily accessible control switches or circuit breakers remote
from the dispensing devices, including any remote pumping system, that will
shut off power to all dispensing devices in the event of an emergency.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-6)
§ 118.07 STORAGE OF LIQUID WASTES.
   Crankcase drainings and flammable or combustible liquids shall not be dumped
into sewers, streams or adjoining property, but shall be stored in tanks or
drums outside any building until removed from the premises.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-7)
§ 118.08 PROVISIONS SUPPLEMENTAL.
   The provisions of this chapter are intended to be supplemental to any
provisions of ordinances of the city relating to the public health and safety
and are intended to impose more stringent standards on the construction and
operation of self-service stations.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-8)
CHAPTER 119: TAXICABS
Section
   
119.01   Defined
   
119.02   License; permit required
   
119.03   Application for license
   
119.04   Fee for license
   
119.05   Inspection of vehicle prior to licensing
   
119.06   Issuance; term; display
   
119.07   Liability insurance
§ 119.01 DEFINED.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definition shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   TAXICAB. Any vehicle carrying passengers for hire.
(Prior Code, § 3-9-1)
§ 119.02 LICENSE; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   Taxicabs. All drivers or operators of taxicabs within the city shall,
before driving or operating a taxicab upon the streets, alleys or public ways
of the city, first obtain a license therefor from the City Clerk.
   (B)   Vehicles for hire.
      (1)   Permits for the driving and operating of such motor vehicles for
hire within the city shall be issued to any person of good moral character
attested to by the affidavit of two resident freeholders of the city who have
not had their motor vehicle operator’s license or commercial chauffeur’s
license revoked by the Commissioner of Public Safety of Oklahoma or his or her
counterpart in any other state within three years immediately prior to the date
of the application, and who has not been convicted of a felony, which
information shall be attested to by the Chief of Police according to his or her
best knowledge, who shall:
         (a)   Exhibit to the City Clerk proof of his (or her) being the holder
of a valid commercial chauffeur’s license issued by the state; and
         (b)   Submit to the City Clerk a recent photograph not less than one
inch by one inch and not larger than two inches by four inches in size for
attachment to a permit to operate such motor vehicle.
      (2)   Such photograph shall be attached by the City Clerk to the permit
for such driver and said permit shall be permanently and visibly displayed at
all times in the taxi or motor vehicle operated by said driver for hire.
(Prior Code, § 3-9-2)
§ 119.03 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   In order to obtain said license, the said applicant shall file with the City
Clerk a written application stating that he or she has never been convicted of
violating any of the rules of the road of the state or been charged and
convicted in any city of violation of any of the city’s ordinances relative to
operating motor vehicles upon the streets, alleys, avenues or public ways of
any city or town within the state, and that he or she has not been convicted in
any court for the commission of a felony within the preceding ten years and
that he or she has not been confined in any penal institution for the
commission of a felony within the preceding ten years.
(Prior Code, § 3-9-3)
§ 119.04 FEE FOR LICENSE.
   The fee for such license shall be as set by the City Council for each
taxicab and each additional license. Licenses shall extend from May 1 until
April 30 the following year, and full license fee must be paid for any part of
such year. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-9-4)
§ 119.05 INSPECTION OF VEHICLE PRIOR TO LICENSING.
   No vehicle shall be licensed as a taxicab until it has been thoroughly
inspected by the Chief of Police or such other official as the Mayor and City
Council may direct, and found to be in a safe, satisfactory and sanitary
condition for the transportation of passengers. All such licensed taxicabs
shall thereafter be inspected in the same manner quarterly between the first
and fifth of January, April, July and October of each year. If any vehicle
licensed as a taxicab is involved in a collision or accident, notice thereof
shall be given to the Mayor and City Council or to such other official as they
may direct, and an inspection shall be made of the taxicab before it can be
again used in service. The report of all such examinations shall be filed with
the Mayor and City Council.
(Prior Code, § 3-9-5)
§ 119.06 ISSUANCE; TERM; DISPLAY.
   Upon making satisfactory showing to the Mayor, the City Clerk shall issue
said license. The license shall continue for and during the period of one year
from the date of the issuance thereof, and said license shall be in conformity
with the licenses issued in other cities within the state, and shall have
pasted thereon a picture of said operator and the license number shall appear
in bold numbers in the upper right-hand corner thereof. No taxicab shall
operate upon any of the public streets, alleys, avenues and public ways of this
city without the display of said license.
(Prior Code, § 3-9-6)
§ 119.07 LIABILITY INSURANCE.
   Upon an application being granted, the applicant shall, before the license
is issued, take out liability insurance in a company licensed to do business in
the state and to be approved by the Mayor and City Council, in a sum not less
than $100,000 for each person, $300,000 each accident for personal injuries and
a sum of not less than $50,000 property damage for each taxicab licensed, not
cancelable without ten days’ written notice to the city. The applicant must
also file competent evidence with the Mayor and City Council that the policy
covers the period for which a license is to be granted. (Refer to
Appendix A following this code of ordinances.)
(Prior Code, § 3-9-7)
